nodes.name: Claude — Plan Routes
nodes.notes: continueOnFail so a Claude API failure doesn't kill the whole workflow with no response ever sent back — retrying is left entirely to the orchestrator (orchestrator/run_session.js), which classifies retryable vs non-retryable errors; n8n's own blind retry-on-fail is intentionally not used here — see Parse Route Plan for how the error is turned into a clean {error: ...} reply instead of a raw n8n 500.

nodes.name: Claude — Compare
nodes.notes: continueOnFail so a Claude API failure doesn't kill the whole workflow with no response ever sent back — retrying is left entirely to the orchestrator (orchestrator/run_session.js), which classifies retryable vs non-retryable errors; n8n's own blind retry-on-fail is intentionally not used here — see Parse Comparison for how the error is turned into a clean {error: ...} reply instead of a raw n8n 500.

nodes.name: Input Guardrail Passed?
nodes.notes: TRUE branch (blocked) skips the Claude call entirely and goes straight to Parse Resolution with the block info already attached — the suspect payload never reaches the Claude HTTP node at all, not just discarded after the fact.

nodes.name: Claude — Resolve Fields
nodes.notes: Same continueOnFail/retry-left-to-caller reasoning as the other two Claude nodes. This call happens mid-route on the worker's own clock, so it also has a shorter timeout (60s vs 90s) — a route is already mid-flight waiting on this.

nodes.name: Verify Input Guardrail Passed?
nodes.notes: TRUE branch (blocked) skips the Claude call entirely and goes straight to Parse Verification with the block info already attached — same shape as the Resolve flow's own guardrail branch.

nodes.name: Claude — Verify Quotes
nodes.notes: Same continueOnFail/retry-left-to-caller reasoning as the other Claude nodes, and the same 60s mid-route timeout as Claude — Resolve Fields — this call happens on the worker's own clock too, waiting to finish extracting a route's results.
